headline: US Third-Quarter Weekly Earnings Growth Lags Inflation at 1.5%
summary: US weekly earnings grew by 1.5% in the third quarter, continuing to trail prevailing inflation rates and squeezing real consumer household income.
why: Real wage dynamics determine US consumer purchasing power, personal savings rates, and macroeconomic growth.

impacts.name: US Consumer Discretionary
impacts.why: Earnings growth lagging inflation reduces household discretionary spending capacity.
